aatrox.why: Everything reduces to an empowered auto (P) whose cooldown is hit-triggered, a three-part ramping recast with a sweetspot (Q), a two-hit skillshot (W), an attack-reset dash (E) and a flat AD buff (R); the fiddly part is P's cooldown refreshing off every hit landed, not any one ability's shape.

ahri.why: Q/W/E are plain casts (Q's return trip needs a positional assumption for the double hit) and R is a self-timed triple recast; P is a pure heal. All fit the primitive vocabulary with no bespoke rotation logic.

akali.why: P's empowered auto only arms after Akali exits a ring formed where her ability landed, a movement-gated proc rather than a plain trigger, and E/R both dash-recast toward a marked point with pass-through/flip geometry; sequencing these positional recasts for max DPS is the hardest part.

akshan.why: Heroic Swing is a three-stage hook/swing/jump combo firing repeated shots during a terrain-bound dash that interleaves with his other abilities, well beyond a primitive combination; Comeuppance's charge-then-volley with missing-health and crit scaling adds further custom logic.

alistar.why: Q and W are plain casts; Trample is a DoT that stacks up to arm a bonus-damage finisher on the next attack, which is the only tricky part. P and R never touch damage.

ambessa.why: Everything reduces to standard primitives: a stack-and-consume passive that empowers autos, a two-part Q combo (Cunning Sweep into Sundering Slam), and a free second E application off her passive dash; the hardest call is that her 70-energy actives on 9-14s cooldowns plausibly outrun a 200 energy bar despite the passive's attack-triggered energy refund.

amumu.why: Cursed Touch is a damage-taken amp on the target (from attacks or R), Despair is a toggled DOT scaling off the target's max health, and Q/E/R are cooldown nukes; the only wrinkle is Q's two stocked charges letting it fire twice early in the 15s window.

anivia.why: Q's initial bolt plus in-flight recast, E's double damage when the target is 'Iced' by Q/R, and R's ramping toggle-dot that can drain even a full mana bar all fit listed primitives; the fiddly part is threading the shared 'Iced' mark between three abilities and R's per-second mana cost actually running dry.

annie.why: Q/W/R are plain cooldown nukes and Pyromania/Molten Shield only add a stun and a shield that a damage-only dummy fight never reads, but Tibbers is a controllable pet that keeps attacking on its own for up to 45s, which needs its own attack-timer logic beyond a generic pet-or-summon primitive.

aphelios.why: Five weapons each swap in a distinct basic attack and Q effect with independently timed cooldowns, moonlight ammo forces weapon cycling, Crescendum accumulates chakram stacks and resets the attack timer on catch, and a Sentry pet attacks on its own; the weapon-queue logic itself is the hard part, not any single effect.

ashe.why: Ranger's Focus is a stack-gated empowered attack with an explicit attack-reset, Frost Shot converts crit chance into flat guaranteed on-hit damage, and Volley's single-target cap (only the first arrow hit counts) is the one geometry assumption; nothing here needs champion-specific control flow.

aurelionsol.why: Stardust is a permanent in-fight stack that boosts Q's damage and E's execute threshold and decides which R version fires, while W pauses Q's channel when E/R are cast during flight and auto-resumes it afterward with a damage-amp and free cooldown; that cross-ability sequencing needs champion-specific logic, not just independent per-ability primitives. Hardest part: assuming a pre-fight Stardust count and modeling the Q channel's interrupt/auto-resume through W/E/R casts.

aurora.why: Spirit Abjuration is a target-stack proc that reads the target's max health, Twofold Hex is a mark-then-recast bolt that scales with missing health, and W/the rest of R are pure mobility/stealth the dummy fight never reads; none of this needs champion-specific logic beyond the listed primitives.

azir.why: Azir's real basic attack is relayed through a Sand Soldier (a line thrust at 50% on-hit effectiveness) that Q and E also consume/refill as ammo, so a generic pet or ammo primitive alone can't reproduce the relayed-attack damage math; P needs an enemy turret to ever trigger, so it does nothing in a turretless dummy fight.

bard.why: W, E and R deal no damage at all (shrine heal, terrain corridor, pure stasis/stun) and Q is one flat bolt (the secondary hit needs a second enemy, which a 1-dummy fight never has); the only real work is Meeps, an ammo-capped on-hit proc whose per-hit damage, stock cap and regen rate all key off a permanent Chime count the simulator has to assume for a level-16 snapshot.

belveth.why: Void Surge has four separately-cooled directional charges instead of one cooldown, Royal Maelstrom is a channel that auto-targets lowest-health-% with its own attack count, and the ultimate's True Form is gated on Void Corals that a solo stationary-dummy fight never generates plus pre-fight Lavender stacks - the coral/form gating needs bespoke setup beyond a simple stance flag.

blitzcrank.why: Q is a single-target nuke that locks him out of attacking while it flies and lands, W is a flat attack-speed steroid, E is a critable empowered attack that resets the swing timer, and R layers a plain-cast AoE burst on top of a passive that stacks on-hit and burns one stack a second as a lightning tick; all standard combinations, no separate mechanism needed.

brand.why: Ablaze is one shared mark/DoT (target-stacks + dot on P): any ability applies it, a 3rd stack detonates for max-health damage, and W deals bonus damage while it is up. The hardest part is R's bounce, which needs an assumed single-target hit count (positional-assumption); otherwise it is plain casts on cooldown.

braum.why: Concussive Blows is a target-stack proc (attacks and Q) that also adds a timed bonus-damage rider on attacks right after it triggers, Q and R are plain nukes, and W/E are pure resistance/damage-reduction with no damage output; all of it fits the listed primitives.

briar.why: Blood Frenzy is a shared forced-attack state (onhit AoE + AS/MS buff) that W or R can enter and that casting E explicitly cancels early, with Snack Attack as a nested empowered attack only usable inside it; that cross-ability cancellation/sequencing is the hard part, not any single primitive.

caitlyn.why: Headshot is an attack-count empowered attack with crit-scaling damage, also triggerable by E's net hit without consuming stacks; R channels briefly then lands a similarly crit-scaled hit. W's bonus-Headshot trigger needs the target to step on a trap, which never happens against a stationary dummy, so it's inert.

camille.why: Hookshot only ever unlocks Wall Dive by attaching to terrain, and this fight has none, so E never fires and drops out of the rotation entirely; what's left (Q's timing-gated double-cast into true damage, W's inner/outer cone split plus a %max-health nuke, R's %current-health onhit window) fits recast-or-multipart, positional-assumption and conditional-damage.

cassiopeia.why: P is pure movement-speed scaling. Q and W deal all their damage as poison DoTs with no upfront hit; E is a cheap nuke on an unusually short 0.75s cooldown whose bonus damage requires the target already poisoned, and spamming it that fast plausibly exceeds a level-16 mana pool within 15s; R is a plain cast.

chogath.why: Q/W/R are plain nukes (Carnivore is an on-kill heal/mana effect the dummy fight never reads), and Vorpal Spikes is an attack-resetting 3-charge empowered attack whose damage reads the target's max health and Cho'Gath's permanent Feast stacks, which also feed Feast's bonus-health ratio; a starting stack count covers both.

corki.why: Every piece maps to a named primitive (E's channel stacks a resist shred while ticking, R is a 4-charge ammo gun where every 3rd shot is a Big One and attacks refund its recharge by a crit-chance-scaled amount); Valkyrie's patch count depends on dash distance, hence positional-assumption.

darius.why: Hemorrhage is a stacking bleed that also grants a timed AD buff on reaching 5 stacks, W is a crit-eligible attack-resetting empowered attack, R is true damage scaled by the target's Hemorrhage stacks, and Q's inner/outer split needs a positional assumption; Apprehend's active is a pure non-damage pull.

diana.why: Q marks the target and E consumes the mark to nearly reset its own cooldown, but that is a plain target-stacks plus cooldown-manipulation combo; the passive's attack-speed buff and stack-and-empower cleave are ordinary steroid/empowered-attack primitives.

draven.why: Catching a returning Spinning Axe both refills a 2-charge ammo pool on Q and separately resets W's cooldown, and R is its own boomerang with a recast reversal and an Adoration-scaled execute; that catch-driven cross-ability coupling is more than a primitive combination.

drmundo.why: Q, W and E all spend the same health pool, and E's bonus damage scales with Mundo's own missing health (up to 70%), so the highest-damage rotation order (spend health via Q/W before E) needs champion-specific sequencing rather than generic cost-gating; W is also a charge that auto-detonates or can be recast early.

ekko.why: Timewinder's grenade can hit the dummy on both the outbound and returning pass, which is the only geometry assumption; Z-Drive Resonance is ordinary target-stacks and Parallel Convergence's passive is a below-30%-health on-hit rider, so the kit composes from primitives without a form, pet, or weapon system.

elise.why: R swaps her entire Q/W/E kit between Human and Spider Form, and Spiderlings are a separately-summoned pet (stored by human-form casts, fighting on their own attack timer in spider form) - a generic form-or-stance plus pet-or-summon pairing can't reproduce that storage/summon handoff without champion-specific logic.

evelynn.why: Demon Shade is an inactivity timer (4s without acting) whose regain resets E's cooldown and swaps it into a stronger Empowered Whiplash, including possibly on the fight's opening cast; that idle-driven empower/reset loop isn't a clean cooldown-manipulation or empowered-attack primitive since it hinges on gaps in the rotation itself.

ezreal.why: Every piece maps to a plain primitive: Q is a plain-cast that shaves cooldowns, W marks the target for a later on-hit-or-ability detonation, and P is an ordinary attack-speed stack; nothing needs champion-specific sequencing.

fiddlesticks.why: Whether Fiddlesticks opens the fight disguised as an Effigy decides if the first Terrify gets its fear/double-damage state, and Terrify's damage/threshold doubling against an already-feared target is a target-state read; Bountiful Harvest's channel, ticks and cooldown refund are otherwise ordinary primitives with no forms, pets or weapon system.

fiora.why: Vitals is a timed appear/expire state machine (1.75s to arm, 13.25s to linger, one active at a time, directionally gated) rather than a simple stack counter, and R changes its availability by opening all four at once; that interaction is the hardest part and needs champion-specific logic beyond the listed primitives.

fizz.why: P only reduces damage taken. Q and R are plain casts (R's tiered damage also needs an assumed lure travel distance). W stacks a permanent on-hit DoT rend, an empowered next-attack, an attack-reset, and a temporary on-hit bonus window if the target survives - all standard primitives, just several on one slot. E (Playful/Trickster) is a recast pair that briefly channels him untargetable before landing the same splash either way.

galio.why: P is a periodic empowered auto whose reduced-crit AD ratio can crit and whose cooldown is cut by landing an ability; Q's two converging windblasts raise whether one dummy takes both hits before the max-health tornado dot; W is a charge that recasts into channel-time-scaled AoE damage; R is a long channel that (with no allies present) has to self-target to land its burst. All map onto listed primitives, but the interactions are dense enough to keep confidence at medium.

gangplank.why: Powder Keg is a charge-based ammo system that must be placed then separately attacked to detonate (spending an auto-attack on the keg instead of the dummy), with chained multi-keg explosions depending on placement geometry, and it resets/feeds Trial by Fire's periodic empowered attack; that action-economy trade-off is the hardest part and isn't reducible to the generic primitives alone.

garen.why: E is a self-looping, recastable channel that locks out attacks, ticks repeatedly, gains spins from bonus attack speed, can crit, and stacks a resist shred every 6th hit; Q is a plain empowered-attack/attack-reset and R is a missing-health true-damage nuke. Hardest part: whether Q's attack can land while E's channel is blocking basic attacks isn't spelled out.

gnar.why: Gnar auto-transforms Mini/Mega mid-fight off a Rage meter built from combat, then locks out of transforming again for 15s after reverting, swapping Q/E/R to different abilities (sharing cooldowns) and only unlocking R's damage in Mega form; timing that transform within a 15s fight needs champion-specific logic, not just a generic form toggle.

gnarbig.why: This is only the Mega half of a rage-gated, forced dual-form kit: P's transform timing, the 15s Mega duration draining automatically, the post-revert tired lockout, and cooldowns shared with Mini Gnar's different abilities need dedicated state logic beyond a generic form swap. Once transformed, the four Mega abilities are themselves plain melee AoE casts (Q refunds cooldown on pickup); R's slot also carries Mini's purely defensive passive.

gragas.why: Q's damage/slow ferments up to 150% over its first 2 seconds before a timed recast detonates it, W is a short channel that arms a %max-health empowered attack, and E refunds 40% of its own cooldown on a hit that will always land on the one dummy. All of it reduces to named primitives with no special-case logic.

graves.why: P is a 2-shell magazine whose basic attack fires 4-6 pellets that stack extra damage on one target, with crit changing both pellet count and per-pellet damage, and E cancels/refreshes the reload while resetting the attack timer and shaving its own cooldown per pellet landed - a specific pellet/reload state machine, not a generic ammo count. Q and R are plain casts (Q has a delayed second detonation; R's splash needs an assumption about whether the single target also eats it).

gwen.why: A Thousand Cuts' max-health scaling triggers off attacks, Snip Snip's center hits, and Needlework alike; Snip Snip banks Snippy stacks into extra snips and Needlework's multi-needle recasts need the assumption that every needle in the barrage lands on the one dummy. Skip 'n Slash is an ordinary empowered-attack/reset/refund kit, with no forms, pets or ammo.

hecarim.why: Warpath converts bonus movement speed into AD, Rampage ramps its own damage and cooldown down on repeated hits, W is a flat AoE DOT, and Devastating Charge is a crit-eligible, attack-resetting empowered attack whose bonus scales with an assumed dash distance; R lands as one flat AoE hit.

heimerdinger.why: Q deploys persistent turrets that fight on their own timer (pet-or-summon) gated by a 3-charge kit, and W's rocket volleys can land several of their five (or twenty) rockets on the same single dummy, so positional-assumption decides how many connect. Needs bespoke logic because R deals no damage itself: it swaps the very next Q/W/E cast for a distinct upgraded ability (a stronger timed turret, a 4x rocket wave, or a bouncing grenade) rather than just buffing numbers.

hwei.why: Q/W/E are each a toggle into one of three separately-costed, separately-cooldowned sub-spells (a 3x3 form-or-stance grid), and R is only castable outside any mood, so choosing which sub-spell to fire each slot is champion-specific ability-order logic, not a primitive combination.

illaoi.why: Almost all her damage routes through autonomous Tentacle pets: P spawns them on terrain the dummy fight doesn't have, Q/W/R command them to slam in sync with diminishing returns for hitting one target repeatedly fast, and a Vessel target gets attacked on the tentacles' own separate timer instead. E's Spirit is a copied decoy with the target's stats that echoes a share of damage back to the real target, which has no matching primitive at all.

irelia.why: Every piece (stacking AS/onhit passive, a mark applied by E/R and consumed by Q for a cooldown cut, a hold-to-scale channel on W, a two-blade convergence on E) maps onto one or more listed primitives; the hardest part is threading the Unsteady mark's cooldown interaction across P/E/Q, but it stays a mark-and-consume pattern rather than needing separate logic.

ivern.why: Daisy is a separate controllable pet with her own attacks and ability that does most of Ivern's fight damage, which is more than a bonus-damage primitive can express; Friend of the Forest is jungle-camp-only and never applies against a champion-flagged dummy, so it drops out entirely.

janna.why: Tailwind converts bonus movement speed into onhit magic damage that also feeds Zephyr's own damage formula, Howling Gale is a charge-then-recast nuke, and Eye of the Storm/Monsoon are shields and knockback/heal with no direct damage except the minor self-AD rider while Janna holds her own shield.

jarvaniv.why: Martial Cadence is a %current-health onhit proc with its own internal cooldown, Q/E/R are plain casts (Q also sheds armor), and W is pure slow-and-shield. The Q-into-flag dash/knockup combo only changes mobility and CC, never damage, so it needs no extra primitive.

jax.why: Two concurrent on-attack stack systems (P's attack-speed stacks and R's empower-every-Nth-hit passive) plus W's empower charge that either a basic attack or Leap Strike can consume are all named primitives; the hardest part is that W's charge can be spent by two different actions, but it stays a single empowered-attack window rather than separate logic.

jayce.why: Jayce carries two entirely separate Q/W/E kits (melee Hammer vs ranged Cannon) that R swaps between, each with its own cooldowns and a different on-transform empowered attack (a damage rider in Hammer, a resist-shred rider in Cannon); Cannon's own Shock Blast also combos through its Acceleration Gate for bonus damage. This needs real stance-tracking logic, not just a generic form-or-stance flag.

jhin.why: Whisper's 4-round clip/reload replaces normal attack speed with converted AD, and the guaranteed-crit 4th shot reads missing health, which is real ammo-system logic rather than a generic attack; R is its own 4-recast channeled cannon with the same missing-health scaling. Q's bounce/kill-chain and W's mark degenerate to plain hits against a single dummy.

jinx.why: Q toggles two weapons with different attack behavior (Pow-Pow stacks attack speed on hit; Fishbones spends mana per attack for modified, crit-eligible AoE damage), but picking and holding the better one for the fight fits a generic weapon-or-ammo-system; P's takedown payoff never triggers against one dummy. The remaining hard parts are geometry assumptions: R's distance-traveled scaling and E's trap-contact timing.

kaisa.why: Living Weapon evolves Q, W and E independently once item-stat thresholds are met, changing missile count, stack size/cooldown-refund and windup/stealth respectively; separately, Plasma is a shared 5-stack counter fed by two different increment sizes (autos +1, Void Seeker +2 or +3) that swaps a ramping on-hit for a missing-health nuke on overflow. That cross-ability conditional upgrade plus a variable-increment shared counter with a threshold payoff swap is more than the listed primitives cleanly compose.

kalista.why: Q/E carry all the damage: Rend is on-hit target-stacks that E consumes for burst, with a kill-reset cooldown refund. Sentinel's Soul-Mark bonus and the entire ultimate require an Oathsworn ally, which the no-allies dummy fight never provides, so W and R contribute no damage here; Martial Poise is a pure mobility passive.

karma.why: Mantra (R) itself deals no damage; it arms whichever of Q/W/E is cast next with a bonus effect, which is not the same as the empowered-attack primitive (that covers basic attacks, not spells) - no listed primitive covers 'a charge that empowers the next different ability cast'. Deciding when to pop Mantra and into which spell is the hardest part and needs champion-specific logic; E is pure shield/speed with no damage.

karthus.why: P (Death Defied) requires taking fatal damage, which a dummy that never fights back can never deal, so it never triggers and is left out. The rest is a clean mage kit: Q is a spammable nuke, W's magic-resist shred only lands if the simulator assumes the wall is placed to overlap the stationary dummy, and Defile's per-second mana cost (it turns itself off if unpayable) makes E's uptime a genuine resource-budget question against Q's spam.

kassadin.why: Mana is a hard constraint: Riftwalk's cost doubles per stack (up to 4) while its damage ramps too, so resource-budget and ramping-per-cast together gate how often R fires; Force Pulse's cooldown is cut by Kassadin's own casts (cooldown-manipulation) and Nether Blade is a plain onhit-rider/empowered-attack/attack-reset passive-active pair. The joint mana scheduling across four costed abilities is the hardest part, but it stays a combination of listed primitives.

katarina.why: Sinister Steel's AoE slash and Shunpo-cooldown refund fire when Katarina retrieves a ground dagger left by Q, W or R, and Shunpo's blink explicitly prioritizes daggers first - a positional reset loop with no matching primitive, so it needs bespoke tracking of dagger state and blink priority. Voracity's takedown-triggered CDR can't matter against a single dummy, so it's excluded. R's per-dagger damage separately scales with bonus attack speed and fires reduced-effectiveness on-hit effects.

kayle.why: All four level-up thresholds (1/6/11/16) are already spent and permanent at level 16 (ranged, always-Exalted, fire wave, full Zealous), so the passive collapses to a fixed always-on onhit rider instead of live stack tracking; Starfire Spellblade's missing-health empower and Q's shred are ordinary primitives.

kayn.why: Kayn permanently locks into one of two forms that outright replace damage formulas (Rhaast turns R's flat+%bonusAD into %max-health plus a self-heal, and adds a %max-health term to Q) and change cast times/cooldown interactions, while Shadow Assassin's on-combat-entry passive converts a percentage of ALL damage dealt into bonus magic damage for 3s - a mechanic outside the primitive vocabulary. The simulator needs two distinct per-form kits, not one generic combination.

kennen.why: Every mechanic maps cleanly onto a primitive: Mark of the Storm is target-stacks that gates W's damage (a mark condition), Electrical Surge is a crit-capable every-4th-attack proc, E is a dash-then-recast that trades into an attack-speed-cap-breaking buff, and R ramps 10%-per-strike target-stacks. The judgment call is whether 40-80 energy actives on 4-13s cooldowns outrun a 200 energy bar despite the kit's several small energy refunds.

khazix.why: Which abilities get evolved is a build-time choice (assume Q/W/E's damage evolves over R's stealth evolve); against a single allyless dummy the isolated-target bonus is always active, not a real assumption. The trickiest part is Unseen Threat re-arming an empowered attack each time Void Assault's stealth is (re)activated rather than off a plain cooldown.

kindred.why: W detaches Wolf to auto-attack independently for 8.5s on his own attack-speed-derived timer while Lamb keeps acting normally, which is a genuinely separate concurrent attack timeline rather than something one driver's rotation can express. P's Mark stacks are a pre-fight assumption that feeds Q's attack speed, E's damage and W's cap, and E's third-mark pounce scales off crit stats on top of missing health.

kled.why: Mounted/Dismounted is a full form swap sharing one health pool between Kled and Skaarl: dismounting disables E and R and swaps Q for Pocket Pistol, which this input never describes, so a real damage number for the dismounted kit is missing. Mounted Q/E each add a same-damage recast, W is a recharging 4th-attack proc scaling off target max health, and R's hit scales with both charge distance and target max health.

kogmaw.why: R's mana cost ramps 40/stack up to 400 on a 1-2s cooldown, which plausibly outpaces a full mana bar inside 15s and forces a fallback to autos/Q/E - a resource-budget/ramping-per-cast combination rather than unlimited spam; its damage also branches (linear missing-health scaling below 60%, else a flat +100% step under 40% max HP), covered by conditional-damage plus execute-or-threshold. P's on-death explosion can never trigger since the dummy never damages the champion.

ksante.why: All Out is a mid-fight form swap with its own rules: it changes Q's and E's cooldowns, strips Path Maker's CC in favor of channel-scaled true damage, and adds a whole new armor/MR-to-damage bonus on Dauntless Instinct - a stance with separate behavior, not a flag. Nearly every ability also converts K'Sante's own bonus armor/MR/health into damage, and Ntofo Strikes empowers every third cast off a 2-stack meter.

leblanc.why: R recasts whichever of Q/W/E she cast most recently, reproducing that spell's full behaviour (including Q's mark or E's two-part chain-and-fracture); tracking last-ability-cast to pick R's effect is champion-specific ability-order logic, not a primitive. The passive's clone never triggers since the dummy never damages her.

leesin.why: Every non-ultimate ability is a two-part cast sharing one cooldown (Sonic Wave into Resonating Strike, which scales with the target's missing health; Tempest into Cripple), which recast-or-multipart and conditional-damage cover. W (Safeguard/Iron Will) is pure shield and omnivamp and Cripple is a pure slow, so a damage-only rotation skips or no-ops them; energy is genuinely tight across a full Q combo, matching the energy-user case for resource-budget.

leona.why: P's mark is only ever consumed by an ally's damage, and this fight has no allies, so it never fires and needs no primitive. Q is a standard empowered next-attack with a reset; W, E and R are plain casts that hit on a short fixed delay.

lillia.why: Dream Dust is one shared DoT any ability applies (dot on P), and R requires it on the target, then puts them to sleep in two timed phases (drowsy then asleep) so that the next hit consumes the debuff for bonus damage - a cross-ability proc like Brand's Ablaze, expressible via conditional-damage. Q's outer-edge true damage and W's epicenter bonus both need an assumed hit position; Prance is movement speed only.

lissandra.why: Q/W/E are ordinary plain casts; R's enemy-cast stun is pure CC but its spreading ice field is a DoT, and the self-cast half is a pure defensive heal a damage rotation would never pick. P needs another nearby enemy champion to already be dead, which can't happen against a single dummy, so it never triggers.

locke.why: Everything is a mark/consume or empower/recast pattern the primitives already cover (Q's up-to-three recasts stacking Soul Nails, consumed by the next attack or E); R's execute threshold just needs an assumed permanent Sealed Champion count. Confidence is tempered by how many primitives stack on Q and E together.

lucian.why: Lightslinger arms an extra, crit-eligible basic-attack shot after every ability cast, which also feeds Relentless Pursuit's per-hit cooldown reduction; Vigilance never triggers since there are no allies to heal/shield Lucian and nothing in his kit immobilizes an enemy. R is a channel firing repeated shots whose count scales with crit chance, an unusual but well-defined formula rather than bespoke logic.

lulu.why: R has no damage at all (health/size/knockup only) and W's enemy branch is pure CC a damage-maximizing cast would skip against a dummy, so only its self-cast attack-speed buff matters. P's on-hit bolts and Q's dual bolt are plain damage; E's enemy cast is a plain-cast burst that also pulls Pix away, briefly suspending P's on-hit bolts - the one open detail.

lux.why: Illumination is a 6-second mark that Q/E/R apply and that a basic attack or Final Spark consumes for bonus magic damage, which is a clean target-stacks/conditional-damage/onhit-rider combination. E is a timed recast-to-detonate zone and W is a pure ally shield with no enemy interaction.

malphite.why: Since the dummy never damages Malphite, his Granite Shield (P) never breaks, so W's passive bonus armor is permanently tripled for the whole fight - a fixed always-on multiplier to precompute rather than a live shield-uptime simulation. E/W's damage ratios scaling off his own armor are ordinary formula inputs, not a distinct primitive.

malzahar.why: W banks a stack every time Q, E or R is cast (cap 2, from casting other abilities, not attacking) and then summons that many extra Voidlings staggered 0.5s apart, each an independent pet with its own attack timer and duration; that cross-ability charge accumulation feeding a variable pet count is more than a generic pet-or-summon.

maokai.why: Sap Magic only triggers below 95% max health, which can never happen since the dummy never damages Maokai, so it contributes nothing beyond being a plain heal. Sapling Toss is a chasing pet whose travel time and brush-empowerment need a positional assumption, and Nature's Grasp is a 5-bramble wall where how many of the five hit the one dummy also needs assuming.

masteryi.why: Double Strike is a capped self-stack that arms an empowered double attack, and Alpha Strike is a lockout cast that re-marks the same lone target several times (an explicit multipart detonation) and can itself crit; Meditate never deals damage so a damage rotation would never use it, and Highlander's kill-reset can't trigger against one dummy.

mel.why: Overwhelm is a stored-damage bank (not a simple counter) fed by every attack and ability, growing by a per-stack formula and detonating its whole bank on the next hit once it would exceed the target's current health - that dynamic, cross-ability, current-health-gated payoff goes past a generic stack/conditional-damage read. W is also moot here: its only damage is reflecting an enemy projectile, and the dummy never attacks, so it is fully defensive in this fight.

milio.why: Fired Up! is a self-buff that W/E/R can grant Milio (he counts as his own ally target) which arms bonus magic damage plus a burn on his next attack or ability hit against an enemy - modeled as timed-self-buff plus empowered-attack plus dot, though consumption by either an attack or Q (not just an attack) is broader than empowered-attack's usual scope. Q's own damage lands only from the post-bounce explosion, whose center is offset from the initial hit, so it needs a positional assumption about whether the target is still inside it.

missfortune.why: A standard on-hit/poke kit: Q's bounce off a single dummy and R's 6-projectile waves are ordinary positional assumptions, and Love Tap marking into Strut's cooldown refund is a plain onhit-rider feeding cooldown-manipulation. Nothing needs champion-specific sequencing.

monkeyking.why: W's clone is an autonomous pet with its own attack timer that also mirrors Crushing Blow's bonus hit, Nimbus Strike's attack speed and every Cyclone cast at a reduced damage scalar - a pet with its own timer mirroring the whole kit, not just a generic summon. Q is an empowered attack that also shreds armor, refunds its own cooldown per hit and resets both attack timers; R is a recastable channel dealing target-max-health-scaled DoT; E is a plain burst plus a timed attack-speed buff.

mordekaiser.why: Obliterate's single-target bonus always applies since only one dummy exists, and Darkness Rise's 3-stack payoff is a self-buffed DoT scaling off the target's max health. Realm of Death's damage-relevant part is just a 7s armor/MR shred (target-debuff); its stat-steal from the target is otherwise inert against a dummy with no offensive stats to take, and Indestructible never deals damage.

morgana.why: W is a missing-health-scaled ticking zone whose own cooldown shrinks every time Soul Siphon triggers off any ability hit; R is a latch-then-delayed-second-hit tether. Since the dummy never moves and CC/mobility are ignored, the tether can never break early, so the second R hit always lands with no extra assumption needed.

naafiri.why: Up to 2-5 Packmates (by level) fight alongside Naafiri for the whole fight and each explicitly deal a cut of R's damage too, so the count and uptime of several concurrent pet attack timers matters directly, not just one temporary pet window; this is the pet-with-its-own-attack-timer case even more than a single pet. The input also only cross-references 'see Pets' for their own stats rather than giving them, which caps confidence.

nami.why: P only buffs allies (irrelevant with none present). W's bounce alternates between enemies, allies and Nami herself, but with no allies and only one enemy it can only ever land once on the dummy, so it reduces to a plain-cast; Q and R are ordinary delayed-impact nukes. E blesses the next 3 attacks-or-ability-casts with bonus damage, which is the empowered-attack primitive even though it can also arm a spell rather than just an auto.

nasus.why: Siphoning Strike's permanent farmed stacks need an assumed pre-fight count (infinite-scaling), Spirit Fire is a delayed hit plus a lingering armor-shred DoT, and Fury of the Sands is a timed self-buff that adds its own max-health-scaled DoT and halves Q's cooldown. Wither and Soul Eater never deal damage in this fight.

nautilus.why: P and W are onhit procs (W's gated by a self-shield window and split into an immediate plus delayed half), Q is a dash-nuke that locks him out mid-flight, E's three self-centered waves raise how many catch one stationary target, and R chases the target leaving trailing eruptions before a guaranteed final impact - a distance/hit-count assumption the vocabulary's positional-assumption is meant to cover. R's chase-and-wake geometry is the main source of doubt.

neeko.why: P (the disguise/Sho'Ma system) is pure identity and vision play with no damage of its own, so it needs no primitive at all. Q's up-to-two rebloom always triggers here since the dummy always counts as a champion, W is a standard 2-stack self-buff arming an empowered attack, and R is a windup-then-leap channel ending in a guaranteed AoE landing hit.

nidalee.why: R fully swaps Q/W/E for a separate Cougar-form kit (Takedown, Pounce, Swipe) with its own cooldowns, and the Hunted mark applied by human-form Q/W is read by the cougar-form abilities and also resets R's cooldown; that cross-form combo sequencing is the textbook form-or-stance bespoke case.

nilah.why: Formless Blade converts crit chance into lethality and its own damage scales with crit chance/damage (stat-conversion plus crit-interaction), and a hit empowers her attack speed for 4s; casting it during Slipstream adds a second wave whose connection needs a positional assumption. R is a 1-second channel that locks out attacks and other casts while it ticks, and E is a 2-charge dash that resets her attack timer.

nocturne.why: Everything reduces to a periodic empowered attack, a plain-cast that leaves a bonus-AD trail, a DoT tether and a recast gap-closer; W's attack-speed doubling requires blocking a hostile effect, which a dummy that never casts can never trigger, so it's purely defensive here.

nunu.why: W and R are charge-and-recast channels whose damage (and, for W, its knockup/stun) scale continuously with how long they're held before releasing; E fires a 3-hit volley that marks the target Snowbound for a delayed root+damage proc 3 seconds later, needing an assumption about how many of the volley's hits land and whether the target still counts as 'near Willump' for the follow-up.

olaf.why: Berserker Rage (P) scales attack speed and lifesteal continuously off Olaf's own missing health, not the target's, so conditional-damage doesn't apply; Reckless Swing (E) pays health as its cost, meaning a self-inflicted resource drain both feeds P's scaling and risks Olaf's own survival inside the fight. No listed primitive covers a stat that scales off the caster's own health.

orianna.why: The Ball is one shared positional resource every ability reads or moves: Q parks it at a location, W/R fire from wherever it currently sits, and E's only legal target with no allies is Orianna herself, which drags the ball away from the dummy and changes what W/R hit next. That persistent, cast-order-dependent position is shared state across the whole kit, not a one-off geometry assumption per ability, so it needs champion-specific logic; E's shield/resistances are otherwise pure defense.

ornn.why: Q's magma pillar is terrain Ornn creates himself, and E's dash only gets its second hit plus a stun if it collides with that pillar (or any terrain) - a self-made combo needing cross-ability position/timing tracking, not just one assumption. Brittle is a target-stacks mark that W/R apply and that only an immobilize or silence (E's terrain-stun, or R's recast-collision-stun) can consume for a %max-health nuke, so which abilities can even trigger it depends on that same terrain question.

pantheon.why: P's Mortal Will stacks (from any attack or cast) empower whichever of Q/W/E is cast next with a different bonus each time - flat damage, a 3-hit empowered attack, or a purely defensive buff - so the rotation must choose which ability consumes the stack, which is ability-order logic beyond a generic Nth-cast primitive. Q is a hold-or-quick-release charge with an execute bonus, E is a channel-then-recast DoT, and R is a multi-phase channelled ultimate whose shockwave also needs an edge-vs-center hit assumption.

poppy.why: Every piece is self-contained: Q's smash-then-rupture and R's charge-then-release are ordinary multipart/channel primitives, E's terrain-collision bonus is a positional assumption, and W's whole damage clause needs an enemy dash the stationary dummy never performs, so it is pure defensive-only here.

pyke.why: Gift of the Drowned Ones converts bonus health into AD, Bone Skewer is a channel-then-recast harpoon, Phantom Undertow is a single fixed-delay hit, Ghostwater Dive is pure stealth/mobility, and Death from Below is a clean health-threshold execute; none of it needs champion-specific logic beyond these primitives.

qiyana.why: Almost the whole kit gates its bonus damage behind holding a terrain Element (Brush/River/Rock) gathered via W, and this fight has no terrain: she'd only ever have the one Element auto-granted on spawn, after which Elemental Wrath's execute bonus and Terrashape's on-hit magic damage lose their trigger, and R's damage is specifically described as the windblast's shockwave crossing River/Brush/Terrain, which may never happen at all. Terrain access is a foundational assumption no generic primitive resolves by itself.

quinn.why: Harrier is one mark placed on the target by Q/E/R and consumed by the next basic attack for conditional bonus damage, which also triggers W's attack-speed buff; R is a 2-second channel that unlocks the multipart Skystrike burst. All of it maps onto the mark/channel primitives without needing a pet or form system.

rakan.why: P is a self-shield (plus an out-of-combat recall sync) and E is purely a shield-and-reposition on an ally, so neither ever deals damage. Q, W and R are each a single delayed-impact magic hit with no target-state or stacking wrinkles; R's collide-once clause is trivially satisfied by the one dummy.

rammus.why: W's only damage is a thorns proc that needs the dummy to auto-attack Rammus, and E only damages monsters, so against a champion-counted target both are pure defense/CC. The bespoke part is R: casting it while Q's roll is still channeling makes R also deal Q's collision damage and knock up, i.e. ability order changes what the next ability does, which is one of the explicit needsBespoke triggers.

reksai.why: Fury is earned purely from landing hits (nothing in this kit spends it to cast) and flips Furious Bite into a bonus true-damage attack at max stacks; no primitive covers a caster-side gauge that is read for a threshold conversion rather than gating a cast. Burrow/Unburrow is otherwise a lightweight form toggle whose only damage is Unburrow's burst, and casting R while Burrowed force-exits that form, so some form bookkeeping is still needed; Tunnel is pure repositioning.

rell.why: W is a Mounted/Dismounted toggle where Crash Down only casts while mounted and Mount Up only while dismounted, each flipping the state the other needs - genuine form-swapping with its own cooldowns, not just a buff window. E also explicitly requires an allied champion target, which this ally-less dummy fight may never supply, so whether it centers its explosion on the dummy at all is uncertain.

renata.why: Most of Renata's kit only matters with allies present (W and Bailout's death-save both explicitly can self-target so they still work solo; R only forces enemies to attack by priority and deals no direct damage, moot against a passive dummy). P's %max-health bonus only fires once (it needs the target unmarked, and her own attacks keep refreshing the mark she just applied); Q's recast damage needs a second body to fly through so it never triggers on one target and is dropped; E's converging-rocket description leaves it genuinely ambiguous whether the same lone target can be caught by both the initial burst and the traveling missile.

renekton.why: Fury is a capped self-resource from attacks/casts that, at 50, empowers whichever of Q, W or E's recast is cast next with a bespoke bonus effect (Q's healing/damage, W's third strike, or E's armor shred) - deciding which ability should consume it is a genuine sequencing choice no single primitive covers. The below-50%-health Fury bonus can't trigger since the dummy never damages him.

rengar.why: Ferocity is a shared resource generated by any cast that empowers whichever of Q/W/E is used next at 4 stacks, each with its own distinct bonus effect, so the simulator must choose which ability to spend it on rather than tracking one fixed nth-hit counter; Unseen Predator's leap-attack also depends on a stealth state from R, and Bonetooth Necklace needs an assumed pre-fight trophy count from champion takedowns.

riven.why: Runic Blade is a consumable onhit-rider fed by ability-cast stacks (up to 3, crit-affected) rather than a flat per-attack bonus; Q is a three-charge multi-cast that also resets her attack timer on each cast, so autos and charges interleave tightly, and R is a buff window that unlocks a missing-health-scaling Wind Slash recast. E is a pure dash-and-shield. All of it stays a combination of listed primitives.

rumble.why: Heat is a dual-threshold resource: casting generates it, reaching 50 empowers Q/W/E by 50% (Danger Zone), and hitting 150 disables all ability casts for 4 seconds while granting bonus attack speed and a %max-health onhit instead (Overheated) - managing that meter and its distinct forced combat mode isn't expressible as an ordinary resource-budget or timed buff. E is a 2-charge harpoon stacking an MR shred up to twice, and R's rocket line needs a positional assumption for how much of its field reaches the one dummy.

ryze.why: P converts AP into bonus mana, which Q/W/E all scale off. Q is a plain cast whose cooldown is fully reset by casting W or E and that deals bonus damage if the target carries E's Flux mark; W and E are plain casts (W's own Flux bonus only changes root vs slow, not damage). R's active is a pure team blink/CC utility with no damage and no allies to use it on.

samira.why: Style only adds a stack when a hit lands on a champion different from the previous hit's target; against one dummy she can only ever reach 1 stack, so R (which spends 6 Style) may be permanently uncastable in this exact fight - a generic stacking-self-buff that just counts attacks/casts would get this wrong, so it needs champion-specific gating. Separately, P's missing-health-scaled bonus magic damage rides on blade autos plus three different abilities, and the source explicitly marks a second P entry ('splash coin') as missing data. The immobilize-empowered-attack in P never triggers since nothing in her kit or the fight rules ever immobilizes the target, so it's omitted.

sejuani.why: Frost (built by W/attacks) must reach 4 stacks before Permafrost (E) is even legal to cast on that target, and consuming it grants an 8s immunity to reapplication; separately, landing any stun creates a Frozen mark (P) that the next hit consumes for bonus max-health damage. Two chained, cross-ability stack systems that gate and feed each other are more than a single mark-and-consume pattern.

senna.why: Weakened Soul's mark (applied or consumed by any attack or ability hit) is target-stacks plus conditional-damage plus onhit-rider spanning basic attacks and Q/W/R; Mist is a separate permanent pre-fight AD/range/crit stack needing infinite-scaling's assumed count (its crit-to-lifesteal conversion is excluded since lifesteal never affects damage dealt). Q also shaves a second off its own cooldown on-attack, and Mist Wraith spawning can't matter against a single dummy that doesn't produce them.

seraphine.why: Echo (every 3rd ability cast repeats for free) is a cast counter and Harmony (stored Notes fire on the next attack) is a capped stack that empowers an attack, both ordinary primitives; the only wrinkle is Seraphine starts the fight already at max Echo stacks, so her first cast is already doubled.

sett.why: Every other attack is an empowered Right Punch (nth-hit-or-cast) and Q empowers two more; the hard part is W, whose Grit resource and its damage bonus both come only from post-mitigation damage Sett takes, which a dummy that never fights back cannot generate, so 'full resource' needs a champion-specific starting assumption rather than the generic mana/energy budget model.

shaco.why: Two independent pet/trap systems (the auto-firing box and the clone that later explodes into three more boxes) plus a from-behind Backstab bonus that changes P, Q and E all at once are well beyond a single generic pet or positional primitive. The clone lasts up to 18s and can only die from damage nothing in this fight deals, so whether its explosion/mini-box payoff even lands inside a ~15s fight is unclear.

shen.why: Q deals no direct damage itself; it empowers the next 3 attacks with %max-health on-hit magic damage and (assuming the recall always clips the dummy, per the fight's always-hit rule) grants bonus attack speed too. W is a pure attack-block zone and R a pure ally-shield-and-blink with no listed damage, both irrelevant here (R likely has no valid ally target at all solo). Energy is the real question: Q alone costs up to 100-140 on a 5-8s cooldown and E costs a flat 150, which plausibly outruns a 200 pool despite E's on-hit energy refund.

shyvana.why: Dragon Form (R) is gated by a 100-point Fury resource that generates from time and combat (tripled while transformed) and drains at a fixed rate while active, so how long she stays transformed - and thus how many Dragon-only bonuses on Q/W/E trigger - depends on a bespoke Fury economy rather than a simple toggle; Q also layers a form-gated third cast onto an already multi-part empowered-attack sequence.

singed.why: Poison Trail is a toggled DoT that drains 13 mana/second and can auto-shut-off if Singed can't keep paying it across a 15s fight, which is the one real resource concern; Fling scales off the target's max health. Mega Adhesive and Noxious Slipstream never deal damage, and Insanity Potion is a plain timed AP/regen buff.

sion.why: Glory in Death only triggers on fatal damage to Sion, which never happens against a dummy that never attacks, so P is inert in this fight. Q and R are both charges whose damage ramps with hold time; R also ends the instant it collides with an enemy, so how far Sion starts from the dummy decides whether the 3-second damage ramp is reached - a real positional-assumption swing of up to 3x that still stays inside the primitive model. W's shield is ignored but its recast consumes it for target-max-health-scaled damage; E adds an armor-shred target-debuff.

sivir.why: Boomerang Blade returns through the dummy for a second hit and Ricochet bounces back onto the same lone target once per empowered attack (no other enemies to prioritize) - both are the returning-projectile/multi-hit geometry the positional-assumption primitive is meant for. On the Hunt's per-attack cooldown reduction is ordinary cooldown-manipulation; Spell Shield and Fleet of Foot never deal damage.

skarner.why: Shattered Earth arms three attacks with an Upheaval alternate finisher, and casting Impale while Shattered Earth is active auto-fires Upheaval for free - a real ability-order interaction between Q and R, not just independent primitives. E's only damage clause needs a target to collide with terrain, which this fight has none of, so it never deals damage.

smolder.why: Dragon Practice is a lifetime stack count that needs an assumed level-16 value, and Q alone reads it to unlock three permanent tiers (an extra explosion, arc bolts exploding at max range, and a stacking true-damage burn with its own sub-6.5%-health execute) on top of two separate crit-scaled damage terms and a cast time tied to attack speed; W's repeat-explosion falloff and E's stack-scaled auto-fired bolts add more of the same. This is well beyond a plain combination of primitives.

sona.why: Power Chord's empowered attack adds a bonus that depends on which basic ability Sona cast most recently - only Q's variant (Staccato) adds real damage, W's and E's variants (a debuff on target damage dealt, a slow) do nothing to a dummy that never attacks - so the driver must track cast history, not just stack counts. Aria of Perseverance's stack generation and Song of Celerity's aura both require an ally, so they and W/E are otherwise inert in an ally-less fight.

soraka.why: Almost the entire kit is healing/utility with no ally present to target (P, W and R are pure heals and W requires an allied target that doesn't exist in this fight); only Q's delayed impact and E's cast-then-erupt zone deal damage, both ordinary plain-cast/recast-or-multipart patterns.

swain.why: Demonic Ascension (R) is a resource-gated form: Demonic Energy decays over time but Swain regenerates it faster than it decays while draining any enemy champion, so against a permanently-present dummy the form plausibly never expires once triggered, and it unlocks repeatable Demonflare casts partway through - a resource race and rotation phase change, not a simple timed buff. Q's five-bolt cone also needs an assumption about how many bolts converge on one target.

sylas.why: R (Hijack) copies the target champion's ultimate ability and casts it for its actual damage; a stationary dummy has no real kit or ultimate to copy, so R's payoff is fundamentally undefined in this fight without an arbitrary champion-specific stand-in. That alone forces needsBespoke; the rest (a 3-stack self-buff arming a critable splash attack, a slow-then-delayed-explosion Q, a plain W, and a dash-then-recast E) is ordinary.

syndra.why: Q creates a Dark Sphere prop that W must grab-and-throw to deal any damage at all and that R collects (3 base plus up to 4 still alive) to size its barrage, so W's and R's damage depend entirely on prior Q timing rather than their own cooldowns; Splinters of Wrath also needs an assumed pre-fight stack count (85 from leveling plus combo-earned splinters) that gates each ability's Transcendent bonus, including R's execute at 100.

tahmkench.why: P's flat magic bonus on attacks and Q is already folded into Q's own listed damage; its stacks only matter at exactly 3, which is Devour's cast requirement (Q's own 3-stack payoff is just a stun). W is a channel that blinks in for AoE damage and refunds on a hit. R is grab-then-recast: Devour makes the target untargetable for up to 3s with no damage, then Regurgitate hits for damage scaled off the target's max health. E is pure defense (grey health/shield).

taliyah.why: Q creates a zone under itself that empowers its own next cast into a different Boulder nuke, and E's up-to-4 stone detonations (with per-detonation falloff) only trigger when W's or R's pure-knockback (both deal zero damage themselves) drags the target across the stone field, so E's real damage depends on an assumed W/R combo path rather than E alone.

talon.why: Every piece is a single documented primitive: P's Wound stacks feed a next-attack bleed, Q's melee-range crit and W's boomeranging daggers are ordinary positional assumptions, and R is a plain outward-then-recast pair. E is pure terrain mobility with no damage.

taric.why: Q (heal), W (armor/shield tether, and moot anyway with no ally present) and R (invulnerability) deal no damage at all; only P's post-cast empowered attacks and E's beam ever touch the dummy, which is about as simple as a kit gets.

teemo.why: Teemo opens the fight stealthed, so his first stealth-breaking action grants a timed attack-speed buff; Q is a plain nuke, Toxic Shot is an onhit magic-damage rider plus a refreshing poison DOT, and mushrooms are the same poison DOT delivered on an assumed guaranteed contact rather than an attacking pet.

thresh.why: Flay's (E) on-hit bonus AD ratio ramps from 0% up to 90-210% the longer Thresh goes without basic-attacking, so maximizing damage means finding an optimal attack cadence rather than applying a flat onhit-rider - a time-since-last-attack ramp with no direct primitive match. Q's Shackle attack-lockout with an early-exit recast, and whether a stationary target is assumed to already be touching one of R's pentagon walls, add further judgment calls.

tristana.why: A clean combo kit: Q is a plain attack-speed steroid, E's charge stacks up from attacks/abilities and can crit-scale, and maxing its stacks resets W's cooldown via ordinary cooldown-manipulation. The on-kill explosion in E never finds a second target in a one-dummy fight.

trundle.why: Q is a standard empowered-attack/attack-reset that also grants Trundle bonus AD (its target-AD-reduction half only matters against an attacker, which the dummy never is); W's attack-speed buff only needs Trundle to stay in his own zone, which a damage-max rotation always does. E deals no damage at all (pure knockback/slow/terrain). R splits into an upfront hit plus a 4-second DoT tail, both scaled off the target's max health, plus a lingering armor/MR shred.

tryndamere.why: Fury converts continuously into crit chance (crit-interaction) and only decays after 8s without dealing or taking damage, which never happens in a continuous fight, so it just ramps up and holds near the cap; R's instant Fury grant mainly speeds up that ramp. Q only heals by spending all Fury (a straight damage loss here, since it also zeroes the crit-chance bonus) and its missing-health AD bonus never applies since nothing ever damages Tryndamere; W only weakens an attacking enemy's AD. Both are dead weight in a damage-only rotation. E is a plain dash-hit whose crits shorten its own cooldown.

twistedfate.why: P only generates gold on a kill, which never affects damage, so it needs no primitive. Q's three fanned cards need an assumption about how many converge on one target. W cycles three card choices, but a damage-maximizing cast always picks Blue's highest-damage empowered attack (crit chance boosts it instead of critting), so it's one fixed empowered-attack payload, not a live decision. E empowers every third attack. R (Destiny/Gate) is pure vision and repositioning with no damage.

twitch.why: Q's 16 s cooldown exceeds the 15 s fight, so it is only ever a pre-fight stealth opener into a flat attack-speed buff; P/W/E form one ordinary stack-and-consume poison chain, and R is a timed AD/range buff whose pierce decay never matters against a single dummy.

udyr.why: Udyr has no ultimate: all four stances share one 1.5s switch cooldown (Bridge Between), but each stance also has its own separate 'Awaken' recast with its own cooldown, and Monk Training layers a universal empowered-attack-plus-cooldown-refund proc onto casting any of the four. That two-tier shared/per-stance cooldown structure plus a passive that hooks uniformly into all four abilities goes beyond a generic form-or-stance primitive. W and E deal no damage at all (heal/shield/mobility) but still occupy the shared stance slot, so they still matter to rotation choice.

urgot.why: P's six independently-cooling shotguns keyed to facing arcs need an assumed rotation to keep presenting a loaded one, and W replaces normal attacks with a fixed, non-crit machine-gun rate for its duration; both are genuine attack-mechanic overrides beyond a primitive combination, plus R's execute has a damage-immunity channel.

varus.why: Living Vengeance is purely kill-triggered so it never turns on against a dummy, but Q and W are tightly bound: W's onhit Blight stacks are detonated by any ability for max-health damage that is itself boosted by how long Q was channeled, W's own active arms Q's next cast with a missing-health nuke at the same channel-scaled rate, and consuming Blight cuts Q/E's remaining cooldowns by up to ~39-58%. That cross-ability scaling and cooldown feedback is real rotation logic, not just a primitive list.

vayne.why: A textbook on-hit kit: Q is an empowered-attack that resets the attack timer, W's third-stack true damage is an ordinary target-stacks proc fed by attacks and E, E's wall-stun is a plain positional assumption, and R is just a timed AD buff plus a Q cooldown-manipulation.

veigar.why: Phenomenal Evil is permanent, uncapped AP per ability hit on a champion, so it needs both an assumed pre-fight stack count and continued live growth as Q/W/R land on the dummy during the fight, feeding forward into every later cast's AP ratio and W's cooldown; that's a broad application of infinite-scaling plus ramping-per-cast rather than a new mechanism. E is pure CC with no damage.

velkoz.why: Every ability feeds one shared Deconstruction stack on the target, which bursts true damage at 3 stacks and separately flags the target as Researched so R's beam deals true damage instead of magic - all cumulative, not order-dependent, so it composes from the mark/channel/ammo primitives. Q's split recast firing perpendicular bolts from the first hit's location makes whether it can re-hit the same lone target a real geometry assumption.

vex.why: Doom only adds crowd control to whichever ability it empowers next, never damage, and Gloom only marks enemies that dash or blink, which a dummy that never moves can never do - so P never touches damage in this fight and Q/W/E/R are ordinary plain casts plus R's mark-and-dash recast.

vi.why: P is a pure shield (its cooldown link to W doesn't matter since P deals no damage). Q is a hold-to-empower charge into a dash-nuke, W is a 3-stack on-hit proc (fed by attacks and Q) that hits for max-health damage, sheds 20% armor and grants attack speed, E is a 2-charge empowered critable attack that resets the swing timer, and R is a dash-grab that lands one delayed hit. All standard combinations.

viego.why: P's Possession needs a takedown, but the only target is the one just killed, so a full kit-swap has nothing left to act on and never changes damage in a one-dummy fight; the rest is ordinary (Q's current-health onhit rider plus a mark-and-second-strike, W's charge-recast dash with attack-reset, R's missing-health nuke).

viktor.why: Hex Fragments/Augments (P) are earned from kills across the whole game, so they resolve to a fixed pre-fight assumption (like a full item build) rather than something to simulate live; most augments (Turbocharge's shield, Magnetize's slow) don't touch damage at all, leaving only Aftershock's delayed E explosion and a Perfect Storm extension that's moot against one target. Gravity Field (W) deals no direct damage, only slow/stun.

vladimir.why: Crimson Rush builds toward a periodic empowered Q rather than a pet or form, and every other piece (W's channel/DoT/health cost, E's charge-and-release nova, R's delayed debuffed burst) is a standard combination; E's 15-bolt nova around himself only ever meets a single stationary dummy with one or two bolts, which is a real geometry assumption.

volibear.why: P's 5-stack self-buff (attack speed) unlocks an onhit lightning rider that keeps hitting the one dummy even though its chain to other enemies never has anywhere to go; Q is the textbook empowered-attack-plus-attack-reset pairing. W marks Wounded and every cast after the first lands the bigger bite damage since its 5s cooldown is shorter than the 8s mark, and E/R are each a single delayed-impact hit (R's Stormbringer buff is otherwise just health/range/size, so defensive-only).

warwick.why: P is a flat on-hit magic proc, Q is a max-health-scaled bite, E's only damage-relevant part is its recast resetting the swing timer (the rest is pure damage reduction/fear), and R is a channelled 3-tick suppression. The one real judgment call is W's Blood Hunt: its passive attack-speed spike below 50%/25% target health is a threshold-gated power step (execute-or-threshold) rather than literal bonus damage, and its active cast grants the same buff unconditionally for 8s (timed-self-buff).

xayah.why: Every feather Xayah shoots (Q, R, and the P/W on-attack procs) plants in the ground for 6s, and E requires at least one planted feather and then recalls all of them with damage falling off per feather already hit on that target. That's a shared, time-limited resource pool fed by four different sources and harvested in arrival order by a fifth ability - a feather queue with individual expiries, not a simple counter a generic primitive covers.

xerath.why: Between Q/W/E/R's mana costs, whether Mana Surge's champion-doubled restoration keeps a full-mana Xerath casting on cooldown for 15s is a real resource-budget question. Rite of the Arcane is a channel with several independently-timed Arcane Barrage recasts whose damage ramps up per successful hit (Arcane Perfection); Arcanopulse is an ordinary charge-then-release. Eye of Destruction's epicenter bonus just assumes the cast is always centered on the dummy.

xinzhao.why: The Challenged mark (P/E/R) only changes range and knockback, never damage, so it needs no primitive; only P's Determination stack-and-burst (fed by attacks and two parts of W) matters. Q arms three empowered attacks that crit normally and shave other cooldowns; W is a slash flurry then a separately-timed thrust, both crit-interacting; E is a plain burst plus a timed attack-speed buff; R is a plain cast that also scales off the target's current health.

yasuo.why: P reworks crit (doubled chance, overflow converts to AD, reduced crit multiplier) but its Flow shield is pure defense. Q is a plain crit-capable cast; its Gathering Storm empowerment only changes the CC (knockup), not the damage, so it needs no extra primitive. E ramps its own damage per stack, but its real cast cadence is capped by a same-target internal cooldown separate from its listed cooldown. R can only be cast on an airborne target - here that means landing Q's empowered knockup first and casting R inside that narrow window, a sequencing requirement beyond a flag check.

yone.why: Steel/Azakana sword alternation is a clean 2-state weapon-or-ammo-system, and P/Q's crit chance doubling, excess-crit-to-AD conversion and reduced crit damage need crit-interaction plus stat-conversion; the third Mortal Steel cast is nth-hit-or-cast empowered. Needs bespoke logic because E doesn't place a simple mark: for 5 seconds it must accumulate 25-35% of every attack's and ability's damage dealt into a running pool, then release the total as one true-damage hit on recast - a weighted-sum tracker, not a countable stack.

yorick.why: Most of Yorick's damage comes from summoned entities: Mist Walkers raised from graves (fed by Q hits, passive nearby deaths, and E's Cursed mark, capped at 4, each leaping and attacking on its own) and the Maiden of the Mist from R, a full separate combat unit whose stats aren't even present in this ability data. That's a pet economy (grave supply, walker lifetimes, a second attacker) rather than one generic pet-or-summon slot.

yunara.why: R's 15-second Transcendent State roughly spans the whole fight and swaps W and E for upgraded, free, faster-cooling versions (with extra cooldown-manipulation bursts on both entry and exit) while auto-activating Q, so the driver must know which kit actually applies for most of the encounter, not just add a buff.

yuumi.why: With no allies in this fight, W (You and Me!) has no valid target and is simply uncastable, which also permanently locks out the large 'Attached'/'Best Friend' damage upgrades on Q, E and R - Q only ever fires its weaker unattached missile, E buffs herself instead of an anchor, and R never gets to steer. P is a pure heal proc with no damage component at all. What's left (base Q, a self attack-speed buff, and R's 5-wave channel, whose wiki total already bakes in one full-damage wave plus four at 25% for a single repeatedly-hit target) is simple, but it is a much smaller kit than Yuumi normally has.

zaahen.why: The Darkin Glaive is a double-strike empowered attack that can chain into a second, differently-empowered attack via its free recast; Dreaded Return is a fixed initial-then-max-range two-part hit rather than a real geometry guess. Aureate Rush needs the edge-vs-center assumption for its bonus damage. Determination's resurrection at max stacks never triggers since the dummy never fights back, so it drops out entirely.

zac.why: P's resurrection-into-bloblets only triggers on fatal damage, which a dummy that never fights back can never deal, so the pet system never appears in this fight and P reduces to pure healing/cosmetics. Q's dual-target displacement/slam bonus likewise needs two different targets that don't exist here, leaving a plain empowered-attack combo; the remaining pieces (W's chunk-fed cooldown reduction, E's charge-release, R's multi-bounce) are standard combinations.

zed.why: W and R each spawn a Shadow that mimics Q and E from its own position 'regardless of range', so a single Q/E cast can hit the dummy up to three times (Zed plus up to two simultaneously-active shadows with different lifespans) - a real pet-attack-multiplier, not independent pet damage. R then stores a share of all damage Zed AND his shadows deal for 3 seconds and detonates it as one hit, so it has to sum across that multiplied output. Energy is also a genuine constraint here (W's passive exists specifically to refund it), unlike an ordinary mana kit.

zeri.why: P replaces her normal attack with a charge-gated zap (executes low-health targets, a full-charge zap scales off max health) built and spent by attacking and casting Q. Q is her real basic attack in practice - it crits, applies on-hit, and its own cooldown is capped and converted by attack speed - but E's Lightning Rounds and R's Overcharged each independently change its round count and damage formula, so one ability has three different modes driven by two different buffs. W's terrain-triggered laser upgrade never fires since this fight has no terrain, leaving only its base single hit.

ziggs.why: P periodically arms an empowered attack and its own cooldown is cut further by casting any ability. Q's bomb can be aimed to detonate immediately on the target, and R's aim naturally lands the full-damage epicenter on a stationary target, so neither needs a geometry assumption; W is a plain throw-then-detonate recast. E scatters 11 proximity mines with steep falloff after the first, and how many actually contact one stationary target is a real geometry assumption.

zilean.why: Q (a delayed-detonation bomb) is Zilean's only damage source; W deals no damage itself but shortens Q's (and E's) remaining cooldown, which is the real lever for more Q casts in 15s. P is an XP/ally-leveling mechanic, E only grants movement speed or slows (no damage on either branch), and R's revive-and-heal needs the dummy to deal fatal damage, which it never does, so all three are defensive-only.

zoe.why: Paddle Star's distance-traveled bonus needs an assumed cast range, but its recast never helps here since the star already detonates on the dummy on the initial cast, so it drops out. Spell Thief's orbiting bolts and shard-mimic active both require enemy summoner-spell casts or dropped shards that a solo dummy fight never produces, so W contributes no damage and More Sparkles always empowers a basic attack instead. Sleepy Trouble Bubble's sleep-consumption bonus is an ordinary marked-target conditional damage read.

zyra.why: Q and E only spawn a Thorn Spitter/Vine Lasher pet if they land on a Seed that Garden of Thorns passively spawned over time or W actively planted from its charge pool, and R then buffs any plants already out into a flurry attack - a real setup-then-convert-then-empower sequence, not independent primitives. The wiki text defers the plants' own attack stats to a Pets section this input doesn't include, so their damage contribution can't be pinned down here.
